|language=en}} ==History== The Kalyani Group was founded by Neelkanth Rao Kalyani. The group's first company, [[Bharat Forge]], was incorporated on 19 June 1961. The group is currently chaired by Neelkanth Rao's elder son, [[Baba Kalyani]]. Some companies are also promoted by his younger son, Gaurishankar Kalyani and his wife, Rohini Kalyani.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-21 |title=Meet Baba Kalyani, MIT engineer & owner of Bharat Forge: Know about his journey, $2.4 billion net worth |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/lifestyle/meet-baba-kalyani-mit-engineer-owner-of-bharat-forge-know-about-his-journey-2-4-billion-net-worth/3095725/ |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}} ==Companies== The group holds key stakes in several companies: === Bharat Forge === {{main|Bharat Forge}} Bharat Forge is the Kalyani Group's first company, founded on 19 June 1961. It manufactures automotive components as well as components for industries such as [[aerospace]], [[railways]], [[marine energy|marine]], and conventional and non-conventional energy. Bharat Forge is the flagship company of the Kalyani Group and has several subsidiaries. Bharat Forge Kilsta, Bharat Forge CDP, and BF Aluminiumtechnik are the company's Europe-based forging units.{{cite web |title=Kalyani Group |url=https://www.kalyanisteels.com/wp-content/uploads/KSLpresn_2015.pdf |website=Kalyani Steels |access-date=27 January 2022}} Defence manufacturer Kalyani Strategic Systems Ltd. is a wholly owned subsidiary of Bharat Forge. Kalyani Strategic Systems owns a 51% stake in Kalyani Rafael Advanced Systems, a joint venture with Israeli defence company [[Rafael Advanced Defense Systems]].{{cite news |last1=Market |first1=Capital |title=Bharat Forge to acquire balance 49% stake in Kalyani Strategic Systems |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/bharat-forge-to-acquire-balance-49-stake-in-kalyani-strategic-systems-121051701099_1.html |website=Business Standard India |access-date=27 January 2022 |date=17 May 2021}} Kalyani Strategic Systems bought a 51% share in the Indian subsidiary of [[Zorya-Mashproekt|Zorya Mashproekt]]. On 9 May 2023, the company signed the acquisition agreement. The acquisition process was finished on 31 December 2023.{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Ritu |date=2024-01-08 |title=India Buys 'Majority Stakes' In Ukrainian Engine Firm As Ukraine War 'Holds-Up' Indian Navy Warship |url=https://www.eurasiantimes.com/big-news-india-buys-majority-stakes-in-ukrainian-engine/ |access-date=2024-01-10 |website=The EurAsian Times |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Gope |first=Koushik |date=2023-12-07 |title=BHARAT FORGE LTD. Acquire of 51% stake in Zorya Mashproekt India Private Limited by Kalyani Strategic Systems Limited |url=https://ismdu.com/bharat-forge-ltd-acquire-of-51-stake-in-zorya-mashproekt-india-private-limited-by-kalyani-strategic-systems-limited/ |access-date=2024-01-10 |website=ISMDU |language=en-US |archive-date=10 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240110100803/https://ismdu.com/bharat-forge-ltd-acquire-of-51-stake-in-zorya-mashproekt-india-private-limited-by-kalyani-strategic-systems-limited/ |url-status=dead }} === Sharp India === Kalyani Telecommunications & Electronics Pvt. Ltd. was incorporated on 5 July 1985 by Bharat Forge. The company manufactured [[black and white]] and [[Color television|colour]] [[television set]]s, and [[videocassette recorder]]s under the brand name Optonica. It became a public limited company on 20 September 1985. The company was renamed Kalyani Sharp India Ltd. on 2 May 1986. Japan's [[Sharp Corporation]] acquired a 40% stake in Kalyani Sharp India Ltd. in 1990. The company was renamed Sharp India Ltd. in 2005.{{cite web |title=Sharp India History {{!}} Sharp India Information |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/sharp-india-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-12212.cms |website=The Economic Times |access-date=27 January 2022 |language=en}} === Kalyani Steels === Kalyani Steels Limited (KSL) was established in February 1973 to fulfill the group's in-house requirements for forging quality steel.{{cite web |title=About us |url=https://www.kalyanisteels.com/about-us/ |website=Kalyani Steels |access-date=27 January 2022}} It manufactures special carbon and alloy steels and alloy steel ingots blooms and billets.{{cite news |title=Kalyani Steels Ltd. |url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/kalyani-steels-322/information/company-history |website=Business Standard India |access-date=27 January 2022}} === Hospet Steel Limited === The manufacturing facility at Koppal, Hospet, Karnataka (known as Hospet Steels) was established in 1998 as a Joint venture alliance between [[Mukand]] and Kalyani Steels. It is an integrated steel plant, spread across 375 acres, with steel-making, finishing and testing facilities.{{Cite web|url=http://environmentclearance.nic.in:80/writereaddata/Online/TOR/0_0_31_Jul_2014_0922476971Annexure-Briefsummaryofproject.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704233048/http://environmentclearance.nic.in:80/writereaddata/Online/TOR/0_0_31_Jul_2014_0922476971Annexure-Briefsummaryofproject.pdf | archive-date=2016-07-04 |title=Kalyani steels limited - Summary|website=environmentclearance.nic.in}} The current capacity of the plant is 2.9 MTPA.It is also knows as ''Kalyani Steels Hospet plant''{{Cite web|url=https://www.oecd.org/industry/ind/latest-developments-in-steelmaking-capacity-2021.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111173338/https://www.oecd.org/industry/ind/latest-developments-in-steelmaking-capacity-2021.pdf | archive-date=2022-01-11|title=Latest developments in steelmaking capacity|website=www.oecd.org}} === Kalyani Carpenter === Kalyani Carpenter Special Steels Ltd. (now Saarloha Advanced Materials Pvt. Ltd.) was established in 1999 as a joint venture between Kalyani Steels and American company [[Carpenter Technology Corporation]].{{cite web |title=Kalyani Carpenter Special Steels Private Limited Company Profile - India {{!}} Financials & Key Executives {{!}} EMIS |url=https://www.emis.com/php/company-profile/IN/Kalyani_Carpenter_Special_Steels_Private_Limited_en_1625195.html |website=www.emis.com |access-date=27 January 2022}} Kalyani Steels' original facility in Pune is now operated by Kalyani Carpenter. === Kalyani Forge === Ellora Engineering Co. Pvt. Ltd. was founded by Neelkanth A. Kalyani in 1979 and began commercial production of forgings in 1981. The company was renamed Kalyani Forge Limited in 1992. Kalyani Forge was the first forging company in India to have the entire press technology as opposed to hammers, which were more common at that time. It is a leader forging and machining critical parts like connecting rods, stub axles, and driveline components.{{cite web |title=Kalyani Group - the Top Leader in Technology & Engineering |url=https://blog.stockedge.com/kalyani-group-challenging-the-conventional/ |website=stockedge.com |access-date=27 January 2022 |date=12 February 2021}} === Kalyani Technoforge === Kalyani Technoforge Limited, formerly Kalyani Thermal Systems Limited,{{cite web |title=Kalyani Technoforge Limited (Kalyani Thermal Systems Limited) |url=https://www.mfg.com/manufacturer/kalyani-technoforge-limited-kalyani-thermal-systems-limited-pune-maharashtra-1443049/ |website=MFG |access-date=27 January 2022}} was established in 1979. It manufactures forgings, machined components, sub-assemblies, and assemblies.{{cite web |title=About KTFL :: About Us :: Kalyani Technoforge |url=http://www.kalyanitechnoforge.com/about-us/about-ktfl.html |website=www.kalyanitechnoforge.com |access-date=27 January 2022 |archive-date=27 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220127034939/http://www.kalyanitechnoforge.com/about-us/about-ktfl.html |url-status=dead }} === Automotive Axles === Automotive Axles Limited (AAL) was established on 21 April 1981 as a joint venture between the Kalyani Group (35.52%) and American company [[Meritor]] (35.52%). It manufactures drive axles, non-drive axles, front steer axles, specialty axles, defence axles, and drum and disc brakes. Automotive Axles has manufacturing plants in Mysore, Karnataka, and Jamshedpur, Jharkhand.{{cite web |title=:: Automotive Axles Limited :: |url=https://www.autoaxle.com/About.aspx |website=www.autoaxle.com |access-date=27 January 2022}} === Kalyani Global === Kalyani Global Engineering Private Limited was established in 1985. It is engaged in the urban infrastructure and construction industry.{{cite web |title=Kalyani Global |url=https://www.bssl.co.in/kalyani-global/ |website=BSSL |access-date=27 January 2022}} === Hikal === Hikal Limited is a specialty chemicals company established in 1988. It manufactures active ingredients and intermediates and provides R&D services for pharmaceutical, animal health, biotech, and crop protection companies.{{cite web |title=Hikal – Who We Are {{!}} About Us |url=https://www.hikal.com/page/who-we-are |website=www.hikal.com |access-date=27 January 2022}} === Kalyani Maxion Wheels === Baba Kalyani established a wheel manufacturing facility in [[Chakan, Pune]], at the request of [[Ratan Tata]], with technology from Hayes Lemmerz. Kalyani Lemmerz Ltd (KLL) was established as joint venture between the Kalyani Group (75%) and Hayes Lemmerz International Inc (25%) in 1996. In 1998, Hayes Lemmerz increased its stake in the company to 85%, with the Kalyani Group holding the remaining 15%.{{Cite web|date=2007-02-23|title=Kalyani Lemmerz vrooms in with $25 m to make car wheels|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/archive/kalyani-lemmerz-vrooms-in-with-25-m-to-make-car-wheels/192551/|access-date=2022-01-27|website=The Financial Express|language=en-US}} In February 2007, Kalyani Lemmerz announced that it would invest $25 million to expand capacity at its wheel manufacturing facility at Chakan.{{Cite news|title=Kalyani Lemmerz lines up $25 m expansion plan|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/companies/kalyani-lemmerz-lines-up-25-m-expansion-plan/articleshow/1676237.cms|access-date=2022-01-27}} Hayes Lemmerz International Inc was acquired by Brazilian company [[Iochpe-Maxion]] in October 2011.{{Cite web|title=StackPath|url=https://www.americanmachinist.com/archive/beyond-the-cutting-zone/article/21895863/wheelmaker-hayes-lemmerz-bought-for-725-million|access-date=2022-01-27|website=www.americanmachinist.com|date=10 October 2011 }}{{Cite web|date=2011-10-06|title=Wheel maker Hayes Lemmerz to be acquired by Brazil's Iochpe-Maxion|url=https://europe.autonews.com/article/20111007/COPY/310079926/wheel-maker-hayes-lemmerz-to-be-acquired-by-brazil-s-iochpe-maxion|access-date=2022-01-27|website=Automotive News Europe|language=en}} Kalyani Lemmerz Ltd. was renamed Kalyani Maxion Wheels Ltd. following the acquisition.{{Cite web|title=Maxion Wheels: Pune, India|url=https://www.maxionwheels.com/locations/pune-india|access-date=2022-01-27|website=Maxionwheels|language=en}}{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=August 2023}} === BF Utilities === BF Utilities Limited was established on 15 September 2000 as a result of the demerger of the Investment and Windmills division of Bharat Forge Limited. The Investment business was demerged again from BF Utilities Ltd to a new company called BF Investment Ltd. (BFIL) on 14 January 2011. === Kalyani Investment === On 25 June 2009, Kalyani Investment Company Limited (KICL) was formed through the demerger of the investment business from Kalyani Steels, along with the amalgamation of the "Investment Undertaking" from three subsidiaries of Kalyani Steel: Chakrapani Investments & Trades, Surajmukhi Investment & Finance, and Gladiolla Investments.{{Cite web |date=2022-12-29 |title=This Kalyani Group firm owns Rs 7,150 cr worth 3 Kalyani stocks; its m-cap stands at 90% discount! |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/company-stock/story/this-kalyani-group-firm-owns-rs-7150-cr-worth-3-kalyani-stocks-its-m-cap-stands-at-90-discount-358170-2022-12-29 |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=Business Today |language=en}} === BF Investment === BF Investment Ltd. (BFIL) was established on 14 January 2011 as a result of the demerger of the Investment division from BF Utilities Ltd. BFIL holds stakes in several other Kalyani Group companies. === Baramati Speciality Steels === Baramati Speciality Steels Limited (BSSL) was founded in 2011. It is located in [[Satara district|Satara, Maharashtra]]. === Synise Technologies === Synise Technologies Ltd. is a company focused on [[procurement]] and Selling Services.{{cite web |title=Synise Technologies Ltd. {{!}} Procurement Services {{!}} SCM {{!}} IT Products & Services {{!}} Asset Management Services |url=https://www.synise.com/(S(1s1ymffc1fko0hkfury3sqb3))/Index.aspx |website=www.synise.com |access-date=27 January 2022}} === KCTI === Kalyani Centre for Technology and Innovation (KCTI) is an ISO 17025 [[National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories|NABL]] certified laboratory established in Pune by the Kalyani Group at an investment of $14 million. The lab is recognized by the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]], and by [[Rolls-Royce]] and [[Boeing]].{{cite web |title=Kalyani Centre for Technology & Innovation (KCTI) |url=https://www.bharatforge.com/technology-innovation/kcti |website=www.bharatforge.com |access-date=27 January 2022}} ==Former companies== ===Bharat FC=== {{main|Bharat FC}} Kalyani Group forayed into [[Football in India|Indian football]] by launching a football club named Kalyani Bharat FC on 23 November 2014. The club began competing in [[I-League|I-league]] from January 2015 and was given direct entry to I-league by the AIFF as an initiative to bring corporates into football. Bharat FC was the 2nd team to enter I-league under this initiative after [[JSW Group]]-led [[Bengaluru FC]], which entered the league in the 2013–14 season.{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/i-league/Rozario-to-assist-Watkiss-at-Kalyani-Groups-Football-Club/articleshow/45181835.cms|title=Rozario to assist Watkiss at Kalyani Group's Football Club – Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=17 November 2014 |access-date=5 February 2020}} Bharat FC played only [[2014–15 Bharat FC season|one season]] of the I-League, finishing at the bottom of the table, before closing down.{{Cite web|url=https://www.firstpost.com/sports/pune-fc-and-bharat-fc-shutting-down-is-the-beginning-of-the-end-of-i-league-2397220.html/amp|title=Pune FC and Bharat FC closing down is the beginning of the end of I-League|website=First Post|date=20 August 2015 |access-date=26 March 2021}} === Kalyani Brakes === Kalyani Brakes was a joint venture company in which the Kalyani Group and [[Robert Bosch GmbH|Bosch]] held a 40% stake each. The company manufactured conventional braking systems and components for passenger cars, tractors, three-wheelers, and two-wheelers. Bosch bought out the Kalyani Group's stake in the joint venture in January 2013. Kalyani Brakes was renamed Bosch Chassis Systems India.{{cite news |title=Bosch buys out Kalyani group from Kalyani Brakes |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/bosch-buys-out-kalyani-group-from-kalyani-brakes-105071600006_1.html |website=Business Standard India |access-date=27 January 2022 |date=16 July 2005|agency=Press Trust of India }} === Kenersys GmbH === The Kalyani Group acquired Münster, Germany-based wind energy and design consulting firm RSB Consult GmbH on 3 September 2007 for an undisclosed amount. The company was renamed Kenersys GmbH, an abbreviation for Kalyani Energy Systems.{{cite news |title=Kalyani group buys German energy co |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/power/kalyani-group-buys-german-energy-co/articleshow/2336158.cms |website=The Economic Times |access-date=27 January 2022}} US-based private equity firm First Reserve Corporation acquired a stake in Kenersys in April 2008. Kalyani Group appointed Paulo Fernando, who was previously the CEO of [[Suzlon]] China, as the new CEO of Kenersys in June 2010.{{cite web |title=New Group CEO at Kenersys |url=https://www.windsystemsmag.com/news/new-group-ceo-at-kenersys/ |website=Wind Systems Magazine |date=2 June 2010 |access-date=27 January 2022}} In September 2010, Kenersys was awarded a contract by Bharat Forge to build a 8 MW wind turbine in [[Satara district]], Maharashtra.{{cite web |title=German Kenersys wins 8 MW wind turbine project in India |url=https://renewablesnow.com/news/german-kenersys-wins-8-mw-wind-turbine-project-in-india-100027/ |website=Renewablesnow.com |date=24 September 2010 |access-date=27 January 2022 |language=en}} Kenersys established a wind turbine production plant at [[Baramati]], [[Pune district]] in September 2011.{{cite web |title=Senvion to acquire Kalyani Group wind business |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/senvion-to-acquire-kalyani-group-wind-business/349370/ |website=The Financial Express |date=17 August 2016 |access-date=27 January 2022 |language=en}} In August 2016, the Kalyani Group reached an agreement to sell Kenersys to German wind turbine manufacturer [[Senvion]] for an estimated {{INRConvert|250|c}}.{{cite news |last1=PM |first1=Indulal |last2=Kalesh |first2=Baiju |title=Arpwood-controlled Senvion to buy Kenersys from Bharat Forge founders |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/engineering/arpwood-controlled-senvion-to-buy-kenersys-from-bharat-forge-founders/articleshow/53725199.cms |website=The Economic Times |access-date=27 January 2022}} === Alstom Bharat Forge Power=== Alstom Bharat Forge Power Limited was a joint venture between the French company [[Alstom]] and Bharat Forge. Originally, Alstom held a 51% stake and Bharat Forge held the remaining 49%.{{cite web |title=Alstom Bharat Forge Begins Production at Gujarat Plant |url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/alstom-bharat-forge-begins-production-at-gujarat-plant-766188 |website=NDTV.com |date=26 May 2015 |access-date=27 January 2022}} Alstom's shares were acquired by American conglomerate [[General Electric]] on 25 November 2015 as part of its global acquisition of Alstom's energy business.{{cite web |title=Alstom Bharat Forge JV to Supply Steam Turbine Generator Islands for NTPC's Telangana Power Plant {{!}} GE News |url=https://www.ge.com/news/press-releases/alstom-bharat-forge-jv-supply-steam-turbine-generator-islands-ntpcs-telangana-power |website=www.ge.com |access-date=27 January 2022 |language=en}} Alstom Bharat Forge won a contract to supply two units of 660 MW supercritical coal turbines to [[NTPC Limited]] for a power plant in [[Solapur]], Maharashtra.{{cite web |title=Alstom-Bharat Forge Joint Venture to supply two turbine islands for coal-fired power plants in India |url=https://www.alstom.com/press-releases-news/2012/4/alstom-bharat-forge-joint-venture-to-supply-two-turbine-islands-for-coal-fired-power-plants-in-india- |website=Alstom |access-date=27 January 2022 |language=en}} Alstom Bharat Forge began production of supercritical turbines and generators at a new manufacturing facility at [[Sanand]], Gujarat in May 2016.{{cite web |title=Production starts at Alstom-Bharat Forges new turbine and generator manufacturing facility in India |url=https://www.alstom.com/press-releases-news/2015/5/production-starts-at-alstom-bharat-forges-new-turbine-and-generator-manufacturing-facility-in-india- |website=Alstom |access-date=27 January 2022 |language=en}} The company won a contract to supply two units of 800 MW ultra-supercritical steam turbine generator islands for the Telangana Super Thermal Power Project Phase-1 near [[Ramagundam]]. On 8 November 2016, the board of Bharat Forge approved the exit of the company from Alstom Bharat Forge Power. In March 2017, Bharat Forge announced that it would divest 23% of its shares to GE,{{Cite web|title=Bharat Forge Divests 23% Stake In Alstom|url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/bharat-forge-divests-23-stake-in-alstom-1673213|access-date=2022-01-27|website=NDTV.com|date=24 March 2017 }} and the remaining 26% stake was divested in February 2018 completing Bharat Forge's exit from Alstom Bharat Forge Power.{{Cite web|title=Bharat Forge exits JV with GE|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/stock-markets/bharat-forge/article22869536.ece|access-date=2022-01-27|website=www.thehindubusinessline.com|date=27 February 2018 |language=en}} == Controversy == [[Baba Kalyani]], Chairman of the group, became embroiled in a legal dispute with his sister Sugandha and her husband Jaidev Hiremath concerning control of Hikal Limited, a subsidiary of the Kalyani Group.{{Cite news |last=Skaria |first=George |title=Not just brother vs brother. Bharat Forge to Hinduja, women are fighting for family business |work=ThePrint |url=https://theprint.in/opinion/not-just-brother-vs-brother-bharat-forge-to-hinduja-women-are-fighting-for-family-business/1531252/}} They submitted a case in the [[Bombay High Court]], alleging that Kalyani's move to increase his group's stake by 5% aimed to gain full control, sidelining and ousting them.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-25 |title=Interview {{!}} 'I simply want what my parents left for our family,' says Sugandha Hiremath, non-executive director, Hikal |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/i-simply-want-what-my-parents-left-for-our-family/3100709/ |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2023-04-20 |title=Kalyani trying to oust me from Hikal: Sister |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/kalyani-trying-to-oust-me-from-hikal-sister/articleshow/99627445.cms |access-date=2023-08-29 |issn=0971-8257}} The Hiremaths held 35% (valued at Rs 3,578 crore), while Kalyani possessed 34%. Hiremath contended that Kalyani selectively disregarded a significant 1994 note indicating the transfer of Hikal shares to Sugandha's family. However, Kalyani refuted the 1994 transfer clause in the family arrangement, deeming it a false assertion by Sugandha. He acknowledged the October 1993 agreement mentioning Hikal's transfer to the Hiremaths but asserted it was overridden by the 1994 arrangement.{{Cite news |title=Hikal ownership dispute: Kalyani family spar over 1993 agreement |work=Business Standard |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/hikal-ownership-dispute-kalyani-family-spar-over-1993-agreement-123040400805_1.html |access-date=2023-08-29}} Kalyani also noted that the Taj meeting centered on resolving ownership matters at [[Bharat Forge]] and Kalyani Forge, not acknowledging any Hikal agreement in 1994. InGovern, an advisory firm, expressed concerns about the lack of agreement between conflicting promoter groups due to differing shareholdings, hampering the passage of special resolutions. In response, Hikal accused InGovern of bias and spreading misinformation to damage the company's reputation. Hikal reaffirmed the Hiremath family's status as promoters, dismissing InGovern's claims and emphasizing that the ongoing lawsuit is a shareholder-level issue, unlikely to impact the company's performance.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-09 |title=Inside the ₹1,300 cr spat between billionaire Baba Kalyani and his sister |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/inside-the-rs-1-300-cr-spat-between-billionaire-baba-kalyani-and-his-sister-11683570419864.html |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=mint |language=en}} In 2024, a new front opened in the row between Baba Kalyani and his sister Sugandha. Sameer and Pallavi, children of Sugandha and Jai Hiremath, have filed suit in a Pune court seeking partition of the Kalyani family assets to claim their share of the Kalyani Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) assets.{{Cite web |last=Mascarenhas |first=Rajesh |date=March 27, 2024 |title=Kalyani family feud deepens: Hiremath siblings move court for share in HUF assets |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/kalyani-family-feud-deepens-hiremath-siblings-move-court-for-share-in-huf-assets/articleshow/108799967.cms |website=The Economic Times}} Baba Kalyani, who turned 75, has a net worth of over $4 billion, was removed from his board position at Hikal in January 2024. Kalyani, who still remains the chairman of Bharat Forge, has been sparring with his sister, Sugandha Hiremath, over a family will.{{Cite web |title=Sibling Rivalry: What Is Happening Inside Baba Kalyani Family |url=https://businessworld.in/article/sibling-rivalry-what-is-happening-inside-baba-kalyani-family-512535 |access-date=2024-06-23 |website=BW Businessworld |language=en}} The suit states that while Baba Kalyani has derived several benefits from the 1994 Family Arrangement, he is refusing to meet his obligation to transfer the Hikal shares to Hiremaths.{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.bharatforge.com/ Bharat Forge website] *[https://www.kalyanisteels.com/ Kalyani Steels website] *[https://www.kalyaniforge.co.in/ Kalyani Forge website] *[http://www.kalyanitechnoforge.com/ Kalyani Technoforge website] {{Authority control}} [[Category:Conglomerate companies of India]] [[Category:Companies based in Pune]] [[Category:1961 establishments in Maharashtra]] [[Category:Conglomerate companies established in 1961]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1961]] [[Category:Multinational companies headquartered in India]]

Kalyani Group is an Indian multinational conglomerate, headquartered in Pune, India, founded in 1961. It operates in various key sectors including engineering, steel, automotive and non-automotive components, renewable energy and infrastructure, and specialty chemicals. The group has also expanded its operations into the defense manufacturing sector, which was showcased at the DefExpo 2020.
The group's annual turnover exceeded USD 2.5 billion as of 2011 and has established joint ventures with companies such as Alstom, Carpenter Technology Corporation, Iochpe-Maxion, Meritor, Sharp Corporation, and Rafael Advanced Defense Systems.
